claims.statement: The European Commission says the definitive CBAM regime applies from 1 January 2026 and that EU importers or indirect representatives above the stated 50-tonne threshold must apply for authorised CBAM declarant status.
The official CBAM Registry supports authorisations, reporting, and emissions-data submissions, leaving supplier evidence collection and reconciliation as a distinct upstream control surface.

contrary_evidence: The 50-tonne threshold removes many very small importers from the core obligation.
Customs suites, consultants, and the official registry already cover filing and authorisation.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: co-sell through two customs brokers rather than acquire importers one by one.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 300 importers at 2000 PLN monthly would create 7.2 million PLN ARR before usage fees; strong retention and founder ownership could support net worth above 5 million PLN in years 5 to 8.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 20 hours weekly for a single CN-code cluster, with customs and emissions counsel contracted.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 70% blended gross margin after paying external emissions reviewers for sampled cases.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: under six months if each enabled broker yields five retained 2000 PLN monthly accounts.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 2000 PLN monthly per importer plus 40 PLN per released customs line.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: recurring imports and annual certificate obligations create repeated reconciliation events.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable mill evidence and a code-to-emissions exception graph shared across consented importer relationships
fingerprint.customer: Polish mid-market importers of covered iron, steel, or aluminium inputs and their customs representatives
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Customs brokers, freight forwarders, metals associations, and ERP implementation partners
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Supplier evidence clearinghouse and compliance ledger, sold as SaaS with specialist verification add-ons
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The importer pays for each internally released customs lot plus an account subscription
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A covered lot is approaching customs and its emissions, code, and declarant evidence must reconcile

founder_fit: Carbon data reconciliation uses quantitative and automation strengths.
A customs-broker channel limits broad cold selling.
The initial build fits the founder's capital if confined to one metals niche.
risks: Incorrect CN classification or emissions calculations could create material liabilities.
A customs software incumbent could add the same evidence module.
Supplier verification may require expertise beyond a software-only team.

structure.control_point: Importer-issued CBAM-ready token before a customs instruction is released
structure.critical_dependency: Trustworthy non-EU installation data and correct customs classification

thesis: A supplier-to-importer evidence clearinghouse for covered iron, steel, and aluminium inputs could turn mill emissions evidence, CN-code mapping, authorisation state, certificates, and customs lines into a reconciled quarterly ledger. A Polish importer would release a customs instruction only after the lot has an auditable CBAM state, while non-EU suppliers would reuse verified evidence across buyers.
title: CBAM Emissions Evidence Clearinghouse for Metal Importers
uncertainties: The density of underserved Polish importers above threshold by narrow CN-code family is unknown.
It is unclear whether non-EU mills will provide installation-specific evidence to small buyers.
The 80000 PLN capital figure and all prices and scale numbers below are hypotheses.
